page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 72 vCPUs across 36 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The dedicated CPU cores operate at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and include 24 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66660.83 and a strong Passmark CPU extended instructions test score of 65810.62. Memory read bandwidth is also strong, reaching 3704.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 208.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average at 90.55 GB/sec. Single-core performance is average across stress-ng and Geekbench tests. In terms of specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong performance in ray tracing and database operations, but exhibits weak text generation speeds for large language models, processing 7.23 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, making it highly optimized for network-intensive operations despite the lack of local storage. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU density and strong multi-core throughput offer a balanced resource profile for compute-bound workloads that require high network throughput but do not need local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is suited for workloads such as distributed database operations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, static web serving, and network-heavy compute clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8124M processor. It features 72 vCPUs, 36 physical cores, and 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory, with no local storage or GPU hardware. The instance delivers strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory read bandwidth, alongside a baseline network speed of 100 Gbps. While single-core benchmarks and LLM text generation speeds are average to weak, its strong database operations and multi-threaded processing capabilities make it highly efficient for network-bound compute workloads. It is suited for distributed databases, web serving, and parallel computing tasks.
